question: Why SiO2 and how to realize 2–3 um floorfill in laser-machined Ti cavities
main_conclusion: SiO2 is a traceable MIR optical benchmark, not a demonstrated optimum. Conformal coating and floor-only filling are different manufacturing geometries. No retrieved paper demonstrates a uniform 2–3 um floor-only fill in this exact Ti blind hexagonal cavity.

sources.title: Mid-infrared optical properties of thin films of aluminum oxide, titanium dioxide, silicon dioxide, aluminum nitride, and silicon nitride
sources.verified: Complex n,k measured over 1.54–14.29 um for room-temperature reactively sputtered dielectric films.
sources.limits: Full original paper sample table was not accessible in this turn. The exact 510 nm sample and 2.0 SCCM O2 labels are verified via project frozen provenance/refractiveindex archive metadata, not newly extracted from full original table. Dense sputtered-layer n,k must not be silently reused as measured n,k for porous sol–gel, particulate or organosilica films.

sources.title: Passive radiative cooling below ambient air temperature under direct sunlight
sources.verified: Paper p542 identifies SiO2 absorptivity peak near 9 um from phonon–polariton resonance, within target 8–13 um; material+multilayer interference produces spectral emission.
sources.limits: HfO2/SiO2 multilayer on Ag; not the Ti floorfill architecture. Does not prove silica alone optimizes the whole 8–13 um band or angle selectivity.

sources.title: Thin sol-gel-derived silica coatings on dental pure titanium casting
sources.authors: K. Yoshida, K. Kamada, K. Sato, R. Hatada, K. Baba, M. Atsuta
sources.verified: Sol–gel dipping was applied to pure Ti after an amino-silane pretreatment; abstract gives 120 C treatment and tensile bond strengths above 55 MPa for silica/silica-F films.
sources.limits: Proof of thin coating compatibility and process route; no demonstrated 2–3 um floor-only fill of deep microcavities, no MIR emissivity or optical-constant characterization. Published treatment is not a ready recipe for present rough laser-ablated TA2.

sources.title: Formation and prevention of fractures in sol-gel-derived thin films
sources.verified: Fast drying creates stress and fracture. In this specific study, silica films cracked above a critical 300 nm while organosilica remained crack-free up to at least 1250 nm.
sources.limits: 300 nm is formulation/substrate/process specific, not a universal silica thickness ceiling; still strong evidence against assuming a single-pass multi-micron pure-silica sol–gel film is automatically crack-free.

sources.title: Plasma-assisted ALD for the conformal deposition of SiO2: process, material and electronic properties
sources.authors: G. Dingemans, C. A. A. van Helvoirt, D. Pierreux, W. Keuning, W. M. M. Kessels
sources.journal: Journal of The Electrochemical Society 159(3), H277–H285
sources.verified: On Si, plasma ALD gave 95–100% conformality in AR~30 trenches; growth per cycle ~1.2 Angstrom around 200 C.
sources.limits: Trenches on Si, not laser-ablated Ti; conformality on Ti rough walls/oxidation must be checked. Coats exposed walls/bottom/top rather than bottom alone. At that paper growth rate, 2 um is ~16667 cycles, illustrative only, not a throughput guarantee.

supporting_sources.title: Drying of Ethanol/Water Droplets Containing Silica Nanoparticles
supporting_sources.authors: Jing Shi, Lisong Yang, Colin D. Bain
supporting_sources.verified: Picoliter droplet drying and deposit morphology depend on coffee-ring flow, solvent evaporation and gelation; uniform deposit was demonstrated with selected fumed-silica formulation.
supporting_sources.limits: Not a Ti blind-cavity fill paper. Do not turn the experimental formulation into a ready floorfill recipe.

supporting_sources.title: Sol–Gel-Derived Vinyltrimethoxysilane (VTMS)/Tetraetoxysilane (TEOS) Hybrid Coatings on Titanium Materials for Use in Medical Applications
supporting_sources.verified: Hybrid silane layers on CP Ti Grade 2 and alloys, 8–15 um and no visible cracks, strong adhesion. FTIR includes organic and Si–O groups.
supporting_sources.limits: Organic–inorganic hybrid, not pure dense SiO2. Its apparent thick-film process success cannot validate use of sputtered SiO2 optical constants or high-temperature thermal-emitter stability.

route_comparison.likely_morphology: Wets accessible walls, bottom and top land; meniscus/pooling vary with drainage/drying.
route_comparison.merit: Relatively accessible large-area route; direct pure-Ti thin-coating proof exists.
main_risks: thickness on flat witness does not equal bottom/wall thickness
adhesion depends on cleaning and interface pretreatment
route_comparison.model_action: Treat as coating with measured wall/top/bottom thicknesses, not nominal floorfill.

route_comparison.likely_morphology: Helps displace trapped air and reach cavities; does not make bottom-selective deposition.
route_comparison.merit: Engineering candidate for arrays and wetting verification.
route_comparison.evidence_status: Engineering inference from wetting/infiltration; no exact Ti-cavity process proof found.

route_comparison.route: Inkjet/drop-on-demand or capillary microdispensing of silica sol/NP dispersion
route_comparison.likely_morphology: Potentially controlled solid loading per cavity, but wetting and drying set actual final profile.
route_comparison.merit: Closest experimental route to deliberately local bottom deposition; start few cavities, not mass arrays.
route_comparison.model_action: Reconstruct measured fill profile and effective optical constants; a generic perfect flat floorfill is a screening approximation.

route_comparison.likely_morphology: Planarization plus filling/bridging/pooling tied to viscosity and curing; topography dependent.
main_risks: does not intrinsically give one controlled 2um pad at bottom of every 100um cavity
substrate and material chemistry differ from Ti

route_comparison.likely_morphology: Conformal walls+bottom+top where reaction saturation achieved.
route_comparison.merit: Best calibrated thin-layer control; useful for nanometer/submicron shell route.
main_risks: real Ti surface nucleation and roughness
conformal coating may narrow aperture/bottom and alter cavity geometry

route_comparison.likely_morphology: Film deposition, not selective liquid filling; step coverage depends on transport/geometry/process; sputter may be directional/shadowed.
route_comparison.merit: Dense witness films with optical characterization can be close to source-data preparation.
route_comparison.evidence_status: General deposition inference; no exact present cavity geometry proof retrieved.

engineering_recommendation.first: Use polished Ti witness plus a small laser-cavity array to test one silica coating route and one local bottom-deposition route. Measure actual morphology before locking the FEM material geometry.
measurement: cross-sectional microscopy/SEM and topography of bottom/wall/top
FTIR spectral R/T or ellipsometry on same-process flat witness to derive/fit effective MIR material input
check chemistry after thermal processing and cycling
engineering_recommendation.modeling: If real process coats sidewalls, simulate actual conformal/nonuniform layer rather than continuing to optimize a floor-only abstraction. Keep current floorfill results as controlled numerical screen, not manufacturing validation.

target_solid_volume_example.interpretation: Sub-picoliter solid volume per cavity; delivered liquid volume depends on solids fraction and final porosity. This is geometric scaling, not a dispensing dose.

engineering_recommendation.thermal_note: Low-temperature sol–gel/hybrid processing can retain OH/organic groups; densification or high-temperature use can change material and Ti oxide interface. Select thermal schedule only after process/material characterization; no generic furnace recipe prescribed.
